surfaces.description: Repo-owned markdown docs and generated markdown copies that need link, lint, and secret checks.
notes: Keep human-facing docs in sync with generated markdown copies.
Run the composite docs receipt, then the secret scan, before closeout.

docs-graph is HERE and not only in the pre-push lane: a docs edit that orphaned a page or added a link-only line was caught by the push, after the slice was committed and its closeout had reported completed. The push lane already carried it for exactly this change class; the closeout obligation for the same surface did not, so the only observer of a docs-only regression was the one that runs after the work is done. Exit 3 is tolerated ONLY when awiki is genuinely absent. check_docs_graph reports UNESTABLISHED on that, and the closeout executor fails on ANY nonzero and then stops the plan, so an unmapped 3 would show a docs-graph defect that is not one and would stop check-markdown and check-secrets from running at all. The `command -v awiki` conjunct is load-bearing and was added by review: exit 3 ALSO covers a scanned-document count below the minimum and, through a blanket except, any crash including the gate's own "misconfigured" refusal — a bare `[ $? -eq 3 ]` turned every one of those into a closeout pass.

Markdown source/derived patterns use <dir>/*.md, NOT <dir>/**/*.md: matching is fnmatch (* crosses /), so *.md covers top-level and nested while the bare **/ form misses a top-level <dir>/<file>.md (e.g. packaging/README.md, which previously escaped these checks at closeout) (#331).

surfaces.description: Raw stdout/stderr transcripts committed under a charness-artifacts/probe/<probe-name>-transcripts/ directory, holding the re-checkable output that the sibling probe JSON only excerpts. Scoped to .txt under a *-transcripts/ directory so it cannot silently absorb another attachment extension, matching the audit-evidence-attachments rule.
verify_commands: for path in charness-artifacts/probe/*-transcripts/*.txt; do [ -e "$path" ] || continue; head -n 1 "$path" | grep -q '^\$ ' || { echo "$path: first line must record the command as '$ <cmd>'"; exit 1; }; cmds=$(grep -c '^\$ ' "$path"); exits=$(grep -c '^\[exit=' "$path"); [ "$cmds" = "$exits" ] || { echo "$path: $cmds command line(s) but $exits '[exit=N]' marker(s); every recorded command needs its return code"; exit 1; }; done
notes: A probe JSON marks its values as author extracts; these transcripts are what makes that honest, so the check pins the two things an extract cannot supply: which command ran, and what it returned.

The glob guard uses `|| continue`, matching audit-evidence-attachments. Without it, pruning the last transcript makes the unmatched glob expand literally, and the check fails naming a path that does not exist -- a wrong diagnostic, not a clean pass.

Marker COUNT is compared against command count, not merely presence: a multi-command transcript with some return codes deleted would otherwise pass on a single surviving marker. Both counts are grep over column-0 anchors and cannot separate framing from recorded OUTPUT, so they are forgeable in both directions -- a command whose output contains a line starting `[exit=` (e.g. `tail -n 1` of another transcript) rebalances the counts and hides a missing return code, and output containing a line starting `$ ` fails a transcript that is fine. Nothing checks pairing or order either: `$ a`, `$ b`, `[exit=0]`, `[exit=0]` passes.

The check reads SHAPE, not truth. It cannot tell whether a transcript was captured from the command it names, or captured at the time the probe claims, and it does not bind a transcript to any probe JSON in either direction -- an orphan transcript no probe cites still passes.

surfaces.description: Preserved diffs (*.patch) committed under charness-artifacts/audit/ alongside the audit or spec artifact that cites them. The audit's own *.md prose is covered by repo-markdown; this surface owns only the .patch extension repo-markdown cannot match. Scoped to .patch on purpose: another attachment extension under the same directory should get its own content check rather than inherit a diff parser, so it still trips unmatched_surface_path until someone decides what verifies it.
verify_commands: for path in charness-artifacts/audit/*.patch; do [ -e "$path" ] || continue; git apply --stat "$path" >/dev/null || exit $?; done
notes: Added 2026-08-11 after charness-artifacts/audit/2026-08-11-pickup-deletion-experiment.patch landed with no owning surface and blocked both bundle-readiness gates on `unmatched_surface_path` for four commits.

A preserved diff is a READING, not a patch to apply: the verify command parses it as a unified diff (git apply --stat) and never checks it against the current tree, which has moved on by design. An empty or truncated .patch still fails (git apply exits 128 on unrecognized input), so the check is not vacuous.

check-secrets is listed because a preserved raw worktree diff is the highest secret-carrying artifact class here. Without it a commit touching ONLY a .patch would select this surface alone and plan no secret scan, which is the question `unmatched_surface_path` used to force.
The glob guard uses `|| continue`, not `[ -e ] && {...}`: the latter makes the loop's exit status 1 when the glob matches nothing, so pruning the last .patch would fail the verify with no diagnostic.

surfaces.description: The retired #514/#515/#518 evidence-boundary crosswalk instance and the record that retired it. The crosswalk path is declared here while ABSENT on purpose: the deletion of a proof-surface instance is itself a change that needs an owning surface, and this one's verify command asserts the absence rather than the file.
notes: Retiring the instance is not retiring the capability: `scripts/evidence/evidence_boundary_crosswalk.py`, its validator, and the `skills/public/issue` authorization ingress are unchanged and still exported, so a consuming repo that checks in its own crosswalk keeps the behavior it had. The plugin-projection test is in the verify command BECAUSE of that claim -- without it this surface asserted an export it never checked.

Node ids, not `-k`. A `-k 'a or b'` filter that still matches one renamed test exits 0 while proving half of what the surface claims; a missing node id is a collection error. This repo has a measured history (#586) of a check that passes while no longer reaching what it names.

If a crosswalk instance is ever checked in here again, this surface is the wrong home for it: move the path back to `issue-source-freeze-bundle` and restore that bundle's validator command, because the checked-in artifact would once again be a live closeout-authorization input rather than a recorded absence.

surfaces.description: Recorded external-tool observations used as quality evidence: each fixture pins its command, tool version/commit, exit code, and digests of the captured stdout and stderr.
notes: The verify command proves each fixture is internally consistent with the streams checked in beside it. It does NOT re-run the external tool and does NOT claim the repo routes that tool to a verdict.
A fixture whose `final_consumer` is null is recorded evidence with no executable reader yet; that gap is #518's work, not this surface's claim.

It replaced an inline one-liner that globbed non-recursively, skipped any fixture missing `stdout_path`, and never looked at `stderr_sha256` -- under which the one checked-in fixture carried a 62-character stderr digest, unread since capture.

surfaces.description: Repo-owned specdown executable acceptance specs and their config.
verify_commands: specdown_report_dir=$(mktemp -d); specdown_config=$(python3 scripts/plugin_export/specdown_ephemeral_config.py --repo-root . --out-dir "$specdown_report_dir") || exit 1; trap 'rm -rf "$specdown_report_dir" "$specdown_config"' EXIT; specdown run -config "$specdown_config" -jobs 4 -out "$specdown_report_dir"
notes: Keep executable specs focused on stable operator-facing behavior; avoid adding adapters until setup or JSON extraction repeats.

The checked-in .charness/specdown/ report is derived state; refresh it manually with `specdown run` when specs change (not a sync command: a direct run rewrites the generatedAt timestamp, so it can never no-op). Automated gates run against an ephemeral config from scripts/plugin_export/specdown_ephemeral_config.py so they do not dirty it.

surfaces.description: Repo-owned Python code and tests.
notes: Use targeted tests when iterating, but close out on the strongest standing Python gates the slice touched.
Release-only install/update lifecycle tests are excluded from the standing Python closeout gate and should run for release, packaging, or tool lifecycle changes.
check_test_repo_copy_invariants.py is the fast standalone structural checker (#307): it runs before the broad pytest so test-fixture drift fails at the commit boundary in <1s, not 172s deep.
check_subprocess_form.py is the fast production-spawn form gate (#768): a scripts/ or skills/ spawn outside subprocess_guard fails before the broad pytest, not only at the broad/bundle quality gate.
Shell test fixtures are repo-test source and run the existing shell lint before broad pytest.

scripts source pattern is scripts/*.py, NOT scripts/**/*.py: matching is fnmatch (* crosses /), so scripts/*.py matches both top-level and nested scripts; the bare **/ form matched zero of the all-top-level scripts and silently kept this whole verify set out of scripts closeouts (#331).

surfaces.description: Advisory-interpretation contract meta-validator (#330): the inference-layer surface registry plus every registered Python/prose declaration and its paired consumer reference.
notes: When a new inference-layer surface is added, register it in .agents/inference-interpretation-surfaces.json AND add its declaration file to source_paths here so the contract re-verifies at slice closeout (#330).

The meta-validator is structural and file-granular: it asserts each registered surface emits the 4-field interpretation declaration with non-empty values plus a paired consumer line, and fails closed on any unregistered 4-field declaration. Intra-file inference-vs-verified gating stays owned by the per-surface #322 tests.

surfaces.description: Repo and skill Python that traverses the filesystem must stay gitignore-aware, so a committed non-gitignore-aware scanner does not ship latent until the next push.
notes: inventory-gitignore-scan-hygiene was a full run-quality.sh-only gate, so the #325 standing_doc_provenance_lib.py repo_root.glob debt shipped at #325 closeout and only surfaced at the v0.27.0 push (#328). Pulling the cheap (<1s) scan into slice closeout catches it at authoring time.

Use scripts/*.py (not scripts/**/*.py): surface matching is fnmatch where * crosses /, so scripts/*.py covers both top-level and nested scripts while the bare **/ form misses a top-level scripts/<file>.py (#331).

surfaces.description: Durable Goal Run provider plans, operations, observations, graph snapshots, and evidence-lineage records.
notes: The issue-owned Goal Run provider is authoritative for graph identity, mutation observations, and child evidence; this surface only makes durable files visible to artifact and release planning.
The JSON parse check is syntax proof, not provider or issue-state proof. Active Goal Run reads and mutations require the issue skill's file-backed commands and exact readback.
Ephemeral `.charness/` runtime output is not a durable Goal Run artifact.

surfaces.description: The registry of commands this repo has measured as dominated by a cheaper one, and the gates that read it.
notes: The registry is a DENYLIST of authored claims; nothing here measures a command's cost, so a green gate is not a cheap repo. The full blind class lives in command_dominance_lib.py's module docstring.
An exemption is keyed to a site and requires a reason. It changes a finding's `exempt` flag, never its presence -- an exempt site stays in the report.
